text:
maya: heads up — seeing a sudden spike in GPU pod preemptions in us-west-2-gpupool-3, kubelet/node-network health checks flipping to FAIL and triggering eviction windows :grimacing:

liam: which nodes? any common topology or ToR?

maya: looks like a subset: ip-10-0-3-45, ip-10-0-3-52, ip-10-0-3-59. all on the same rack/NUMA zone and using the same NIC firmware.

maya: kubelet logs (snippet):
```
Mar 15 14:12:03 kubelet[2345]: network health check failed: probe seq mismatch (expected 8 got 3)
Mar 15 14:12:03 kubelet[2345]: node network health: packet loss 35% over 30s, marking node NotReady
Mar 15 14:12:04 kubelet[2345]: evicting pods: non-reclaimable resources: preempting GPU workloads
```

jordan: ran mtr between the affected nodes and a healthy control node — saw intermittent 5-60% packet loss on the east-west path through the ToR, spikes correlate with high conntrack churn. :eyes:

kubelet-bot: alert — 12 pods evicted across 3 nodes in us-west-2-gpupool-3 (auto-detected).

liam: have we changed conntrack/iptables/firmware recently? conntrack exhaustion or asymmetric routing can make probe replies get lost and look like a node net failure. check `/proc/net/nf_conntrack` and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`

maya: ran those: conntrack_count ~ 380k, nf_conntrack_max = 393216 (close to limit). most entries are TIME_WAIT from short-lived control connections (kube-proxy, grpc health checks).

jordan: also noticed RDMA NIC offload + veth overlay on these hosts. sometimes hw offload interacts badly with conntrack when flows are steered to different PFs. quick test: disable offload on one canary with `ethtool -K eth0 tx off rx off` and watch.

kai: any quick mitigation to stop the evictions while we investigate? we need to keep prod GPU jobs running.

liam: temporary mitigations we can try (safe, reversible):
- increase nf_conntrack_max to 800k (`sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=800000`)
- increase kubelet node-monitor-grace / node-status thresholds in the KubeletConfig for the pool (`node-status-update-frequency` and `node-monitor-grace-period`) to avoid transient probe failures causing NotReady quickly
- roll a canary kernel/firmware rollback on the affected rack if the FW was recently bumped

maya: I bumped conntrack_max on a pair of canaries and disabled NIC offload on one. after ~8m the netprobe flaps stopped and no further evictions there.

jordan: confirmed: canary node packet loss dropped from 30% -> 1-2% after offload toggle. suggests offload/firmware bug.

kai: good call. let's apply the kubelet grace change as a cluster-level temporary policy for the GPU pool (10m -> 30m) and roll out the conntrack bump cluster-wide after hours. document rollback steps. :+1:

maya: filing a follow-up: we'll open an infra ticket to coordinate firmware vendor escalation, kernel upgrade test matrix, and a plan to reduce conntrack reliance (longer-lived control channels, backpressure). also will add a health check metric to detect conntrack occupancy.

liam: one more note — long-term we should tune the health probe to use a small UDP probe via the ToR rather than TCP flows that interact with conntrack, or shift probes to the CNI dataplane probe that bypasses conntrack. I'll draft options.

maya: thanks team. I'll post the mitigation playbook + commands in the ticket and schedule a canary rollout.

kubelet-bot: incident ticket created: INFRA-2981 — "Conntrack/firmware induced network probe flaps causing GPU pod preemptions"

jordan: TL;DR: cause looks like conntrack churn exacerbated by NIC offload/firmware -> kubelet net health false positives -> GPU pod evictions. temporary: bump nf_conntrack_max + increase kubelet grace + disable offload per-canary. plan: vendor firmware/Kernel fix + probe redesign.
